migrations.name: 0001_owner.sql
migrations.sql:
-- Additive schema draft. Integrator assigns the next migration number; never
-- replace an applied migration. All epoch timestamps are milliseconds.
CREATE TABLE oa_operators (
 id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, display_name TEXT NOT NULL,
 role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(role IN ('owner','admin','member')),
 status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('invited','active','inactive')),
 version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE oa_bootstrap (singleton INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(singleton=1), claim_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, claimed_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE oa_tokens (
 id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, token_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
 kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(kind IN ('magic','invite')),
 operator_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES oa_operators(id), operator_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
 issuer_id TEXT REFERENCES oa_operators(id), issuer_version INTEGER,
 return_to TEXT NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 consumed_at INTEGER, revoked_at INTEGER,
 CHECK((kind='invite' AND issuer_id IS NOT NULL AND issuer_version IS NOT NULL)
    OR (kind='magic' AND issuer_id IS NULL AND issuer_version IS NULL))
);
CREATE TABLE oa_sessions (
 id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, token_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
 operator_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES oa_operators(id), operator_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
 kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(kind IN ('native','review','oidc','password','dev')),
 source_token_id TEXT UNIQUE REFERENCES oa_tokens(id),
 created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL, revoked_at INTEGER
);
CREATE INDEX oa_sessions_operator ON oa_sessions(operator_id);
CREATE TABLE oa_external_identities (
 issuer TEXT NOT NULL, subject TEXT NOT NULL, operator_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES oa_operators(id),
 PRIMARY KEY(issuer, subject)
);
CREATE TABLE oa_limits (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, window INTEGER NOT NULL, count INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TRIGGER oa_preserve_last_owner_update BEFORE UPDATE OF status,role ON oa_operators
 WHEN OLD.role='owner' AND OLD.status='active' AND (NEW.role!='owner' OR NEW.status!='active')
 AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM oa_operators WHERE role='owner' AND status='active') <= 1
 BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'last_owner'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER oa_preserve_last_owner_delete BEFORE DELETE ON oa_operators
 WHEN OLD.role='owner' AND OLD.status='active'
 AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM oa_operators WHERE role='owner' AND status='active') <= 1
 BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'last_owner'); END;
-- A status/role change invalidates every preexisting session and link, including
-- after a later reactivation. Keep this invariant for direct administrative SQL.
CREATE TRIGGER oa_operator_version AFTER UPDATE OF status,role ON oa_operators
 WHEN OLD.status != NEW.status OR OLD.role != NEW.role
 BEGIN UPDATE oa_operators SET version=OLD.version+1 WHERE id=NEW.id; END;

-- Fresh installs include local dev identity. Apply schema/dev-sessions.sql as a
-- NEW numbered migration in existing stores; it is also safe after this file.
-- A credential minted while signed in with a dev session is recorded here and,
-- like the dev session itself, counts only behind the local key gate.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oa_dev_credentials (
 credential TEXT NOT NULL, id TEXT NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 PRIMARY KEY(credential, id)
);

-- Fresh installs include the additive invitation cancellation ledger.
-- Apply as a NEW numbered migration after operator-auth.sql in existing stores.
-- This durable record is admission state, not an expiring credential. Never prune it.
-- Existing active/inactive operators retain their recorded status: no historical
-- acceptance is inferred. Only a witnessed invited -> inactive transition records
-- an unaccepted cancellation, including direct administrative SQL transitions.
CREATE TABLE oa_invitation_cancellations (
 operator_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES oa_operators(id),
 operator_version INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TRIGGER oa_record_invitation_cancellation AFTER UPDATE OF status ON oa_operators
 WHEN OLD.status='invited' AND NEW.status='inactive'
 BEGIN INSERT INTO oa_invitation_cancellations(operator_id,operator_version)
 VALUES(NEW.id,OLD.version+1)
 ON CONFLICT(operator_id) DO UPDATE SET operator_version=excluded.operator_version; END;
CREATE TRIGGER oa_reject_cancelled_invitation_reactivation BEFORE UPDATE OF status ON oa_operators
 WHEN NEW.status='active' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM oa_invitation_cancellations WHERE operator_id=OLD.id)
 BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'invitation_required'); END;

-- Fresh installs include domain rules and step-up proofs. Apply
-- schema/domain-rules-step-up.sql as a NEW numbered migration in existing
-- stores; it is also safe after this file.
-- A required sign-in provider for an email domain. Sign-ins for that domain by
-- any other route are refused; app owners are exempt.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oa_domain_rules (
 domain TEXT PRIMARY KEY, provider_id TEXT NOT NULL,
 created_by TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES oa_operators(id), created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
-- A step-up proof: an app-local email link sent to the operator's own address,
-- bound to the session that asked and completed only in that session. No
-- foreign key names oa_sessions, which schema/dev-sessions.sql rebuilds.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oa_step_up_challenges (
 id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, token_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
 session_id TEXT NOT NULL, operator_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES oa_operators(id),
 operator_version INTEGER NOT NULL, action TEXT NOT NULL, return_to TEXT NOT NULL,
 created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL, consumed_at INTEGER
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS oa_step_up_session ON oa_step_up_challenges(session_id);

migrations.name: 0005_identity_providers.sql
migrations.sql:
-- Identity providers (OpenID Connect). Apply as a NEW numbered migration after
-- the accounts schema. Every statement is IF NOT EXISTS, so a store that applied
-- an earlier version of this file applies the current one again as its next
-- migration and gains only what it lacks.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oa_oidc_transactions (
  state_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  binding_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  config_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  payload TEXT NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS oa_oidc_transactions_expiry ON oa_oidc_transactions(expires_at);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oa_oidc_limits (
  bucket TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  count INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
-- One pinned link per configured provider. Linking stores the issuer, JWKS URI,
-- client id, endpoints and allowed algorithms; a changed configuration only
-- records a pending re-link, which the owner completes with a step-up proof.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oa_identity_providers (
  provider_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  preset TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('linked','unlinked')),
  issuer TEXT NOT NULL,
  client_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  jwks_uri TEXT NOT NULL,
  authorization_endpoint TEXT NOT NULL,
  token_endpoint TEXT NOT NULL,
  algorithms TEXT NOT NULL,
  token_auth_method TEXT NOT NULL,
  response_iss INTEGER NOT NULL,
  interface_version TEXT,
  linked_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  pending_issuer TEXT,
  pending_client_id TEXT,
  pending_preset TEXT,
  pending_at INTEGER,
  jwks TEXT,
  jwks_fetched_at INTEGER
);
-- Reachability per configured provider, linked or not. A provider that has
-- failed discovery or JWKS for 5 minutes, or answered 404 or a DNS failure, is
-- hidden from the sign-in page until a later check succeeds.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oa_identity_provider_health (
  provider_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  failing_since INTEGER,
  hard_failure_at INTEGER,
  checked_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

-- An undone batch no longer holds its file: staging the same export again starts
-- a new batch. 0014 made file_hash unique and D1 keeps foreign keys on, so the
-- table is not rebuilt; a file staged again after an undo stores its hash with
-- the new batch's id appended, and this index keeps one open batch per file by

migrations.name: 0016_auth_agents.sql
migrations.sql:
-- Preparer keys: an agent reads the inventory and files proposals; a person
-- approves. Only the key's SHA-256 digest is stored; the key itself is shown
-- once at minting. Its owner is the administrator who minted it and is
-- accountable for it. A key confers no session and no administrator right.
CREATE TABLE auth_agent_keys (
 id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, label TEXT NOT NULL, secret_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
 owner_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES oa_operators(id),
 created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL, last_used_at INTEGER,
 renewed_at INTEGER, revoked_at INTEGER, revoked_by TEXT REFERENCES oa_operators(id)
);
CREATE INDEX auth_agent_keys_owner ON auth_agent_keys(owner_id);
-- A proposed change. Filing stores its effect, the target's state and that
-- state's digest; nothing else changes until a person approves, and
-- execution_id marks the one approval that ran it.
CREATE TABLE auth_agent_proposals (
 id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, key_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES auth_agent_keys(id),
 kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(kind IN ('suspend_person','restore_person','invite_person','remove_invitation','add_domain_rule','remove_domain_rule')),
 target TEXT NOT NULL, params TEXT NOT NULL, reason TEXT NOT NULL,
 effect TEXT NOT NULL, target_state TEXT NOT NULL, state_digest TEXT NOT NULL,
 created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK(status IN ('pending','done','rejected','failed')),
 decided_by TEXT REFERENCES oa_operators(id), decided_at INTEGER, outcome TEXT, execution_id TEXT UNIQUE
);
CREATE INDEX auth_agent_proposals_key ON auth_agent_proposals(key_id);
CREATE INDEX auth_agent_proposals_pending ON auth_agent_proposals(status,created_at);

migrations.name: 0017_auth_agent_key_owner_version.sql
migrations.sql:
-- A preparer key ends for good when its owner stops being an administrator.
-- The key records its owner's oa_operators.version at minting; Base's trigger
-- bumps that version on every status or role change, so a key whose recorded
-- version no longer matches is ended and promoting or restoring the owner
-- again does not revive it. Keys minted before this migration keep working
-- only if their owner is an active administrator now; the rest end here.
ALTER TABLE auth_agent_keys ADD COLUMN owner_version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;
UPDATE auth_agent_keys SET owner_version=COALESCE((SELECT p.version FROM oa_operators p WHERE p.id=auth_agent_keys.owner_id AND p.status='active' AND p.role IN ('owner','admin')),0);

-- Machine administration is a separate OAuth namespace, never a person/session.
CREATE TABLE auth_admin_service_apps (
 id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
 client_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
 name TEXT NOT NULL,
 purpose TEXT NOT NULL,
 owner_id TEXT NOT NULL,
 jwks TEXT NOT NULL,
 scopes TEXT NOT NULL,
 resources TEXT NOT NULL,
 allowed_ips TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
 revision INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK(revision>0),
 created_by TEXT NOT NULL,
 created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 revoked_at INTEGER,
 revoked_by TEXT,
 suspended_at INTEGER,
 suspension_reason TEXT,
 last_used_at INTEGER
);
CREATE INDEX auth_admin_service_owner ON auth_admin_service_apps(owner_id);
CREATE TABLE auth_admin_service_assertions (
 service_app_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES auth_admin_service_apps(id),
 jti TEXT NOT NULL,
 expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 PRIMARY KEY(service_app_id,jti)
);
-- Losing accountable human authority persists even when a role/status is restored.
-- A human reassignment is the only operation that clears the suspension.
CREATE TRIGGER auth_admin_service_owner_changed AFTER UPDATE OF status,role ON oa_operators
 WHEN NEW.status!='active' OR NEW.role NOT IN ('owner','admin')
 BEGIN
  UPDATE auth_admin_service_apps SET suspended_at=COALESCE(suspended_at,CAST(strftime('%s','now') AS INTEGER)*1000),
   suspension_reason=COALESCE(suspension_reason,CASE WHEN NEW.status!='active' THEN 'owner_suspended' ELSE 'owner_demoted' END),
   revision=revision+1
  WHERE owner_id=NEW.id AND suspended_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL;
 END;
CREATE TRIGGER auth_admin_service_owner_deleted BEFORE DELETE ON oa_operators
 BEGIN
  UPDATE auth_admin_service_apps SET suspended_at=COALESCE(suspended_at,CAST(strftime('%s','now') AS INTEGER)*1000),
   suspension_reason=COALESCE(suspension_reason,'owner_departed'),revision=revision+1
  WHERE owner_id=OLD.id AND suspended_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL;
 END;

CREATE TABLE auth_delegated_tasks (
 id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, agent_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES auth_delegated_agents(id),
 agent_revision INTEGER NOT NULL, service_revision INTEGER NOT NULL,
 organization_id TEXT NOT NULL, accountable_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES oa_operators(id),
 accountable_version INTEGER NOT NULL, app_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES auth_apps(id),
 app_version INTEGER NOT NULL, native_epoch INTEGER NOT NULL, role_epoch INTEGER NOT NULL,
 effect TEXT NOT NULL, effect_digest TEXT NOT NULL,
 before_role TEXT, before_created_by TEXT NOT NULL, before_created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'requested' CHECK(state IN ('requested','consented','approved','completed','revoked','rejected')),
 revision INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
 consented_by TEXT, consented_at INTEGER, consent_session_id TEXT,
 approved_by TEXT, approver_version INTEGER, approved_at INTEGER, approval_session_id TEXT,
 revoked_by TEXT, revoked_at INTEGER, ended_reason TEXT,

);
CREATE INDEX auth_delegated_tasks_person ON auth_delegated_tasks(accountable_id,state);
CREATE INDEX auth_delegated_tasks_agent ON auth_delegated_tasks(agent_id,state);
CREATE TABLE auth_delegation_assertions (
 agent_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES auth_delegated_agents(id), jti TEXT NOT NULL,
 expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(agent_id,jti)
);
CREATE TRIGGER auth_delegated_effect_immutable BEFORE UPDATE OF agent_id,agent_revision,service_revision,organization_id,accountable_id,accountable_version,app_id,app_version,native_epoch,role_epoch,effect,effect_digest,before_role,before_created_by,before_created_at,created_at,expires_at ON auth_delegated_tasks
 BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'delegation_effect_immutable'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER auth_delegated_agent_ended AFTER UPDATE OF state,revision ON auth_delegated_agents
 WHEN NEW.state!='active' OR NEW.revision!=OLD.revision
 BEGIN
  UPDATE auth_delegated_tasks SET state='revoked',revision=revision+1,
   revoked_at=CAST(strftime('%s','now') AS INTEGER)*1000,ended_reason='agent_changed'
   WHERE agent_id=NEW.id AND state IN ('requested','consented','approved');
 END;
CREATE TRIGGER auth_delegated_person_ended AFTER UPDATE OF status,version ON oa_operators
 WHEN NEW.status!='active' OR NEW.version!=OLD.version
 BEGIN
  UPDATE auth_delegated_tasks SET state='revoked',revision=revision+1,
   revoked_at=CAST(strftime('%s','now') AS INTEGER)*1000,ended_reason='person_changed'
   WHERE (accountable_id=NEW.id OR approved_by=NEW.id) AND state IN ('requested','consented','approved');
 END;
-- This task profile excludes employees with any unrevoked scoped role grant.
-- Once a grant is added, removing it cannot revive earlier task authority.
CREATE TRIGGER auth_delegated_role_added AFTER INSERT ON auth_role_grants
 WHEN NEW.revoked_at IS NULL
 BEGIN
  UPDATE auth_delegated_tasks SET state='revoked',revision=revision+1,
   revoked_at=CAST(strftime('%s','now') AS INTEGER)*1000,ended_reason='person_role_changed'
   WHERE accountable_id=NEW.person_id AND state IN ('requested','consented','approved');
 END;
CREATE TRIGGER auth_delegated_role_changed AFTER UPDATE OF person_id,revoked_at ON auth_role_grants
 WHEN NEW.revoked_at IS NULL
 BEGIN
  UPDATE auth_delegated_tasks SET state='revoked',revision=revision+1,
   revoked_at=CAST(strftime('%s','now') AS INTEGER)*1000,ended_reason='person_role_changed'
   WHERE accountable_id=NEW.person_id AND state IN ('requested','consented','approved');
 END;
-- Generic credential custody excludes this namespace. Internal lifecycle writes
-- may end its backing authority but cannot widen or repurpose it. New keys,

CREATE TRIGGER auth_delegated_credential_immutable BEFORE UPDATE OF client_id,owner_id,jwks,scopes,resources,allowed_ips,expires_at ON auth_admin_service_apps
 WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM auth_delegated_agents a WHERE a.service_app_id=OLD.id)
 BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'delegated_credential_immutable'); END;
